abstract: A UX audit is an expert review of your product's usability. Ours combines a heuristic review, analytics and usability findings into a prioritized fix list with effort estimates, delivered in 2–3 weeks by 1–2 senior designers for $5,000–$15,000.

sections.answer: A UX audit is a structured expert evaluation of a digital product that finds where users struggle, explains why, and ranks the fixes by impact and effort, so teams improve the product without guessing.
sections.body: Unlike usability testing services, which watch real users complete tasks, an audit is run by experienced designers against established usability heuristics, accessibility guidelines and your product analytics.

sections.h2: What does our UX audit include?
sections.answer: Our UX audit includes 4 parts: a heuristic review, an analytics review, an accessibility check, and a prioritized fix roadmap.

items.title: Heuristic review.
items.body: Key flows evaluated against recognized usability heuristics such as Nielsen's 10.

items.title: Analytics review.
items.body: Funnels and drop-off points checked to show where users leave.

items.title: Accessibility check.
items.body: Common WCAG issues flagged across the audited screens.

items.title: Fix roadmap.
items.body: Every finding ranked by impact and effort, with an estimate.

sections.h2: How does the UX audit process work?
sections.answer: The UX audit process takes 2–3 weeks and runs in 4 steps, from agreeing the goals to handing over the prioritized roadmap.

items.title: Kick-off and goals
items.body: We agree the flows, metrics and user groups to audit.

items.title: Review
items.body: Designers run the heuristic, analytics and accessibility reviews.

items.title: Synthesis
items.body: Findings are grouped, evidenced with screenshots and scored.

items.title: Roadmap handover
items.body: We walk your team through the prioritized fixes and estimates.

sections.answer: A UX audit is expert-led and fast; usability testing is user-led and shows real behavior. Most teams run an audit first, then test the riskiest flows with users.

sections.h2: How much does a UX audit cost?
sections.answer: A UX audit costs $5,000–$15,000 and takes 2–3 weeks with 1–2 designers. The price depends on the number of flows, platforms and user groups in scope.
